title: Death of gran crushed by collapsed Shevington home wall 'was preventable'

evidence_packet.title: Death of gran crushed by collapsed Shevington home wall 'was preventable'
evidence_packet.lead: Warnings about the bowing wall were raised almost eight years before Clarice Berry died
evidence_packet.summary: Warnings about the bowing wall were raised almost eight years before Clarice Berry died
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Death of gran crushed by collapsed Shevington home wall 'was preventable' - BBC News Image source, Family handout Image caption, Clarice Berry died after the wall of her home collapsed on to her Published 17 September 2026 Concerns about a bowing wall of a rental property which collapsed and crushed a woman beneath it were reported nearly eight years before her death, a coroner found. Clarice Berry died from chest injuries suffered when the gable wall of her home in in Shevington, Wigan, collapsed on to her in July 2021, trapping her beneath the rubble. The 77-year-old was in the lean-to carport beneath the gable end of the property when the entirety of the gable wall and the upper part of the outer leaf of the end wall, weighing around 3,800kg, collapsed. In a prevention of future deaths report published on Thursday, coroner Bronia Hartley said Berry's husband reported the bowing wall nearly eight years beforehand. Hartley ruled her death could have been prevented in an inquest in July if action was taken after concerns about the wall were repeatedly raised. The home was an end-of-terrace rental property owned by landlord S&G Properties (No 2) Limited and overseen by property management company KMPM. From 2013 onwards, the property showed signs of cavity wall tie erosion, Hartley's report said. Berry reported concerns to the property's previous managing agent, but his report "fell by the wayside" when a new managing agent, Kaye Mackenzie, took over. A property manager from Kaye Mackenzie visited the property in August 2013 and recorded in his notes: "Gable wall big bulge in wall – needs urgent repointing/+rebuild." The same manager visited the property again in March 2016 and noted that the gable "needs repointing". The manager retired when Kaye Mackenzie was wound up

title: Scout Moor: Plans for onshore windfarm scaled back by a third

evidence_packet.title: Scout Moor: Plans for onshore windfarm scaled back by a third
evidence_packet.lead: Developers say the changes to the Scout Moor II scheme follow feedback from residents and consultees
evidence_packet.summary: Developers say the changes to the Scout Moor II scheme follow feedback from residents and consultees
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Scout Moor: Plans for onshore windfarm scaled back by a third - BBC News Image source, Cubico Image caption, The new site is planned for moorland between Rochdale and Rossendale, next to the existing Scout Moor wind farm By Richard Stead and James Fell , North West Published 17 September 2026 Developers have cut the number of turbines proposed for a major wind farm on moorland after reviewing feedback from residents and organisations. Renewable energy firm Cubico Sustainable Investments has reduced the number of proposed turbines at Scout Moor II, between Rochdale and Rossendale, from 17 to 12. The site would be next to the existing Scout Moor wind farm. The revised plans have been submitted to Rochdale and Rossendale councils and will now be subject to a further round of consultation before councillors whether to approve it. Campaign group Friends of the Moorland said it was unlikely the revisions would address all of its concerns. Steve Davison from the group said: "We need to review the plans in detail to come to a considered view but it's unlikely that all of our fundamental objections will have been addressed." Each turbine could be up to 590ft (180m) tall, making them taller than Blackpool Tower. The proposals previously prompted hundreds of objections and opponents warned of the impact on peatland, wildlife and the landscape. Peter Rowe, project lead for Scout Moor II, said the changes were a direct response to feedback from residents and other organisations. "We previously proposed 17 turbines and we're now coming down to 12," he said. "It's not about building as many turbines as possible. It's always about a balance. "We obviously want to maximise clean energy generation and secure energy generation, but equally it needs to be right for the place." Image captio

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Alex Batty, who disappeared for six years after being abducted by his mother as a child, has described feeling a renewed "sense of purpose" after finding work Batty, from Oldham, was declared missing by his grandmother in 2017, aged 11, after his mother and grandfather failed to return him from a holiday in Spain and instead moved to France He spent the following years in isolation before he was spotted by a delivery driver in December 2023 in the foothills of the Pyrenees in the south-west of the country Batty, who is now 20, said his job at a waste management company had given his young family financial security It has been a whirlwind couple of years for Batty, whose teenage years were spent living as a nomad in France His mother, Melanie, who was not his legal guardian and was heavily influenced by conspiracy theories, told him to throw away his passport

title: Work to restore Manchester's Chinatown archway underway

evidence_packet.title: Work to restore Manchester's Chinatown archway underway
evidence_packet.lead: The gateway into Manchester's Chinatown is in need of significant repairs, the city council says
evidence_packet.summary: The gateway into Manchester's Chinatown is in need of significant repairs, the city council says
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Work to restore Manchester's Chinatown archway underway - BBC News Image source, Manchester City Council Image caption, The Grade II-listed landmark was a gift from Beijing to the people of Manchester Published 17 September 2026 Work has started on the restoration of a landmark archway in Manchester's Chinatown. The Grade II-listed feature was a gift from Beijing to the people of the city in the mid 1980s. The gateway into the city's Chinatown is now in need of significant repairs which is estimated to take two years to complete, Manchester City Council said. Councillor Mandie Shilton Godwin said while the arch will be missed during the work "rest assured it will be worth the wait". Image caption, The work on the archway was a "priority", said councillor Mandie Shilton Godwin The work is part of a wider regeneration of the Chinatown area. Improvements have already been carried out earlier this year to make repairs to the large pagoda, new bespoke benches have been installed, and works are planned within the month to make repairs to the smaller pagoda. Shilton Godwin, executive member for clean air, environment and transport, said the arch has been a focal point for the Chinese community in Manchester for generations and ensuring it remains standing proudly for years to come was a "priority". "We know the significance this area holds for many of our residents and that's why we are committing to further investment, ensuring that it's not only a top destination for tourists visiting Manchester, but a community that local people feel proud to live and work in." She added: "During this two-year project we know that the arch will be missed, but rest assured it will be worth the wait." evidence_packet.lead: Courts Girl arrested for 'foolish decision' after England World Cup match, now she's in court 'She apologises for her behaviour' Comments News Kenny Parker and Paul Britton Reporter 06:19, 18 Sep 2026 Updated 06:54, 18 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Anya Hugh A teenage drink-driver prang
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Girl arrested for 'foolish decision' after England World Cup match, now she's in court 'She apologises for her behaviour' Comments News Kenny Parker and Paul Britton Reporter 06:19, 18 Sep 2026 Updated 06:54, 18 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Anya Hugh A teenage drink-driver prang
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Girl arrested for 'foolish decision' after England World Cup match, now she's in court 'She apologises for her behaviour' Comments News Kenny Parker and Paul Britton Reporter 06:19, 18 Sep 2026 Updated 06:54, 18 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Anya Hugh A teenage drink-driver pranged her new car after watching England's football team crash out of this summer's World Cup finals, a court was told Newly-qualified driver Anya Hughes, 18, smashed her Mini Cooper into another vehicle after leaving a pub at 10.30pm following England's semi-final defeat to Argentina in July. A court heard she ran away from the scene, leaving the damaged vehicle, a Fiat 500, behind Hughes, a former care assistant of Smallwood Court, Congleton, Cheshire, returned 30 minutes later after being contacted by police, who traced her through her car registration number. She subsequently failed a breath test and was arrested Inquiries revealed Hughes, who had only passed her driving test in May, had been drinking in a bar in Macclesfield after the match. She went on to insist her foot slipped off the clutch before the crash At Chester magistrates court, Hughes was banned from driving for a year after she admitted drink-driving. She faces a retest before she can get behind the wheel again

evidence_packet.lead: Stockport Stockport care home boss says 'I didn't think a human could fit through' after gran falls to death from bedroom window The inquest into the death of 78-year-old Maureen O'Callaghan is being heard at Stockport Coroners' Court View 2 Images Ma News Chris Slater Senior Rep
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Stockport care home boss says 'I didn't think a human could fit through' after gran falls to death from bedroom window The inquest into the death of 78-year-old Maureen O'Callaghan is being heard at Stockport Coroners' Court View 2 Images Ma News Chris Slater Senior Rep
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport care home boss says 'I didn't think a human could fit through' after gran falls to death from bedroom window The inquest into the death of 78-year-old Maureen O'Callaghan is being heard at Stockport Coroners' Court View 2 Images Ma News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 06:10, 18 Sep 2026 The former manager of a care home where a beloved gran fell to her death from her bedroom window - having previously attempted to climb through - told an inquest he did not believe a 'human being could fit through' Maureen O'Callaghan, who had dementia, died at Berrycroft Manor in Romiley, Stockport, on September 29 last year. The 78-year-old fell through her upstairs bedroom window, having previously attempted to climb out and throwing items from it Ms O'Callaghan's loved ones have told an inquest into her death, being heard at Stockport Coroners' Court, they believe her death was a 'preventable tragedy' Coroner Jyoti Gillearlier earlier heard Ms O'Callaghan moved to Berrycroft Manor in January 2025 to benefit from '24-hour care' at a cost of '£1,600 a week'. Her family said they had spoken to care home staff with safety concerns about the window, but nothing was done about Describing Ms O'Callaghan's death as a 'preventable tragedy', the family said: "She was an integral part of our close family and her loss will stay with us all."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Wigan's home's 'timebomb' 3,800kg wall was reported eight years before collapsing and killing gran Clarice Berry was left buried under 10ft of rubble when the gable end of the semi-detached house in Wigan came down in the summer of 2021 View 3 I Comments News Manchester Evening News 06:08, 18 Sep 2026 Concerns about a bowing wall of a rental property which collapsed and crushed a gran as she hung out her washing were reported nearly eight years before her death, a coroner has said Clarice Berry, 77, was left buried under 10ft of rubble when the gable end of the semi-detached house on Old Lane, Shevington, Wigan , came down on July 18, 2021. She died from chest injuries A coroner previously heard how she was hanging out laundry underneath the lean-to-carport when bricks began to fall before the 'timebomb' wall - weighing around 3,800kg - completely gave way and landed on her Horrified neighbours and passers-by, who said it sounded like a 'bomb had gone off', rushed to the scene and desperately attempted to save Mrs Berry from beneath the debris. The married grandmother-of-six - a retired kitchen assistant - was eventually freed by firefighters and ru Coroner Briona Hartley described the death as 'senseless' and a 'tragedy' at an inquest at Bolton Coroners' Court last year. She slammed the failure by the property landlord to repair the brickwork, which her husband Arthur said he had repeatedly complained about

News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 16:48, 17 Sep 2026 View 2 Images The debt was 'un Salford council has written off more than £600,000 owed by bosses of a once celeb-studded restaurant The town hall leased space at 1 New Bailey to Kiki Concepts Limitedfor Menagerie. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Lillia Lloyd Watson 13 from Bolton, missing girl police appeal LIVE Updated 11 mins ago Missing Lillia search LIVE as mum issues plea to Bolton girl, 13, one week after she vanished - updates An urgent appeal has again been issued for 13-year-o The 13-year-old was last seen boarding the 247 bus at the Trafford Centre at 1.50pm on Saturday (September 12). She had been reported missing a day earlier, having been seen at Piccadilly Gardens bus station just before 11pm that night Earlier this week, her mother issued a heartfelt plea for Lilia to 'come home'. Jessica said: "Lillia, you're not in any trouble, I'm really, really worried. It's been four nights now and you need to be safe. Please come home, we all love you very much." GMP yesterday (Thursday) set up a Major Incident Public Portal for information on her whereabouts as detectives again pleaded for information. Officers say it is unclear how long she was on the bus from the Trafford Centre for or where she got off That sighting is being treated as an important part of the investigation, with cops asking for anybody who was on the bus and remembers seeing Lillia to get in touch. Lillia is 5 ft 5; of slim build; with brown hair and glasses. She was last seen wearing a black zip-up hooded top GMP's Major Incident Public Portal can be accessed HERE

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Destroyed memorial bench was 'final straw' in Salford park plagued by 'crime, drugs, and public sex' Yet the council has decided not to install lighting or CCTV News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 15:09, 17 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Clow CCTV and floodlighting will not be installed in a park plagued by crime where a Holocaust memorial bench was vandalised and thrown into a lake, Salford Council has confirmed A bench in Clowes Park that carried the audio testimony of a Shoah survivor Chaim Ferster was smashed up and dumped in the boating lake in a ‘distressing’ incident in January. evidence_packet.lead: Wigan MP hits out at Leigh terraced house converted to five-bed HMO without planning permission Wigan council has tightened the regulation of shared homes but the applicant claims that previously the conversion 'would have been classed as permitted de Planning permission for a ne
evidence_packet.summary: Wigan MP hits out at Leigh terraced house converted to five-bed HMO without planning permission Wigan council has tightened the regulation of shared homes but the applicant claims that previously the conversion 'would have been classed as permitted de Planning permission for a ne
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan MP hits out at Leigh terraced house converted to five-bed HMO without planning permission Wigan council has tightened the regulation of shared homes but the applicant claims that previously the conversion 'would have been classed as permitted de Planning permission for a newly created HMO in Leigh has been applied for retrospectively Plans published by Wigan council state that the property is an extended mid-terrace house on the eastern side of Leigh Road, around 620 metres north of the town centre The applicant, Sarfat Ahmed, is applying for full retrospective planning permission to the change the use of the building into a single occupancy five-bedroom house in multiple occupation In July, 2025 Wigan council made a borough wide article 4 direction that removed permitted development rights for changes of use from individual houses to small houses in multiple occupation It meant that from August 31, 2025 all HMOs, regardless of size, need planning permission

In the past few weeks, hundreds of streets in the borough have had missed or delayed pick ups of household waste, most of which were described by the council as due to ‘operational issues On September 3, the council apologised for the issues and said it was sending crews out on weekday evenings and Saturdays to try and clear the huge backlog. It is understood that recent sickness levels have seen around 10 drivers had signed off on long-term sick leave, with anoth At that time, the Bolton council website listed 632 streets in the borough where bins had not been emptied in just four days At present, the missed collection list for the past week on the website lists 82 streets with missed collections, however for the vast majority the reason given is ‘no access’ with just five listed as ‘operational issues’ One councillor said many residents were ‘fed up’ of the failure to collect and ‘something is wrong’ that the council was missing so many bins

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Lillia Lloyd Watson 13 from Bolton, missing girl police appeal LIVE Updated 9 mins ago Missing Lillia search LIVE as mum issues plea to Bolton girl, 13, one week after she vanished - updates An urgent appeal has again been issued for 13-year-ol The 13-year-old was last seen boarding the 247 bus at the Trafford Centre at 1.50pm on Saturday (September 12). She had been reported missing a day earlier, having been seen at Piccadilly Gardens bus station just before 11pm that night Earlier this week, her mother issued a heartfelt plea for Lilia to 'come home'. Jessica said: "Lillia, you're not in any trouble, I'm really, really worried. It's been four nights now and you need to be safe. Please come home, we all love you very much." GMP yesterday (Thursday) set up a Major Incident Public Portal for information on her whereabouts as detectives again pleaded for information. Officers say it is unclear how long she was on the bus from the Trafford Centre for or where she got off That sighting is being treated as an important part of the investigation, with cops asking for anybody who was on the bus and remembers seeing Lillia to get in touch. Lillia is 5 ft 5; of slim build; with brown hair and glasses. She was last seen wearing a black zip-up hooded top GMP's Major Incident Public Portal can be accessed HERE

The campervan was pictured being removed from the road on a recovery truck in an image shared this morning (September 18) GMP Wigan says the driver's holiday plans were 'brought to a sudden stop'. A spokesperson wrote on Facebook: "Officers from the Abram Neighbourhood Team have seized this campervan after checks revealed it had no insurance and no valid MOT "It may have been ready for a road trip, but unfortunately it wasn't quite ready for the road. Instead of heading off on an adventure, this campervan is taking an unscheduled stay at our recovery compound "Before setting off, please make sure your vehicle is insured, taxed and has a valid MOT where required. A few minutes checking your documents could save a very expensive detour."

evidence_packet.summary: Courts Girl arrested for 'foolish decision' after England World Cup match, now she's in court 'She apologises for her behaviour' Comments News Kenny Parker and Paul Britton Reporter 06:19, 18 Sep 2026 Updated 06:54, 18 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Anya Hugh A teenage drink-driver prang
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Girl arrested for 'foolish decision' after England World Cup match, now she's in court 'She apologises for her behaviour' Comments News Kenny Parker and Paul Britton Reporter 06:19, 18 Sep 2026 Updated 06:54, 18 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Anya Hugh A teenage drink-driver pranged her new car after watching England's football team crash out of this summer's World Cup finals, a court was told Newly-qualified driver Anya Hughes, 18, smashed her Mini Cooper into another vehicle after leaving a pub at 10.30pm following England's semi-final defeat to Argentina in July. A court heard she ran away from the scene, leaving the damaged vehicle, a Fiat 500, behind Hughes, a former care assistant of Smallwood Court, Congleton, Cheshire, returned 30 minutes later after being contacted by police, who traced her through her car registration number. She subsequently failed a breath test and was arrested Inquiries revealed Hughes, who had only passed her driving test in May, had been drinking in a bar in Macclesfield after the match. She went on to insist her foot slipped off the clutch before the crash At Chester magistrates court, Hughes was banned from driving for a year after she admitted drink-driving. She faces a retest before she can get behind the wheel again

evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Stockport care home boss says 'I didn't think a human could fit through' after gran falls to death from bedroom window The inquest into the death of 78-year-old Maureen O'Callaghan is being heard at Stockport Coroners' Court View 2 Images Ma News Chris Slater Senior Rep
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport care home boss says 'I didn't think a human could fit through' after gran falls to death from bedroom window The inquest into the death of 78-year-old Maureen O'Callaghan is being heard at Stockport Coroners' Court View 2 Images Ma News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 06:10, 18 Sep 2026 The former manager of a care home where a beloved gran fell to her death from her bedroom window - having previously attempted to climb through - told an inquest he did not believe a 'human being could fit through' Maureen O'Callaghan, who had dementia, died at Berrycroft Manor in Romiley, Stockport, on September 29 last year. The 78-year-old fell through her upstairs bedroom window, having previously attempted to climb out and throwing items from it Ms O'Callaghan's loved ones have told an inquest into her death, being heard at Stockport Coroners' Court, they believe her death was a 'preventable tragedy' Coroner Jyoti Gillearlier earlier heard Ms O'Callaghan moved to Berrycroft Manor in January 2025 to benefit from '24-hour care' at a cost of '£1,600 a week'. Her family said they had spoken to care home staff with safety concerns about the window, but nothing was done about Describing Ms O'Callaghan's death as a 'preventable tragedy', the family said: "She was an integral part of our close family and her loss will stay with us all."

evidence_packet.lead: Wigan Wigan's home's 'timebomb' 3,800kg wall was reported eight years before collapsing and killing gran Clarice Berry was left buried under 10ft of rubble when the gable end of the semi-detached house in Wigan came down in the summer of 2021 View 3 I Comments News Manchester Eve
evidence_packet.summary: Wigan Wigan's home's 'timebomb' 3,800kg wall was reported eight years before collapsing and killing gran Clarice Berry was left buried under 10ft of rubble when the gable end of the semi-detached house in Wigan came down in the summer of 2021 View 3 I Comments News Manchester Eve
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Wigan's home's 'timebomb' 3,800kg wall was reported eight years before collapsing and killing gran Clarice Berry was left buried under 10ft of rubble when the gable end of the semi-detached house in Wigan came down in the summer of 2021 View 3 I Comments News Manchester Evening News 06:08, 18 Sep 2026 Concerns about a bowing wall of a rental property which collapsed and crushed a gran as she hung out her washing were reported nearly eight years before her death, a coroner has said Clarice Berry, 77, was left buried under 10ft of rubble when the gable end of the semi-detached house on Old Lane, Shevington, Wigan , came down on July 18, 2021. She died from chest injuries A coroner previously heard how she was hanging out laundry underneath the lean-to-carport when bricks began to fall before the 'timebomb' wall - weighing around 3,800kg - completely gave way and landed on her Horrified neighbours and passers-by, who said it sounded like a 'bomb had gone off', rushed to the scene and desperately attempted to save Mrs Berry from beneath the debris. The married grandmother-of-six - a retired kitchen assistant - was eventually freed by firefighters and ru Coroner Briona Hartley described the death as 'senseless' and a 'tragedy' at an inquest at Bolton Coroners' Court last year. She slammed the failure by the property landlord to repair the brickwork, which her husband Arthur said he had repeatedly complained about

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics 'Historic moment' for Number 10 North as first international leader visits Andy Burnham in Manchester 'We are the closest of friends, and I look forward to further strengthening that friendship' Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 22:30, 17 S Andy Burnham will host Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin in Manchester on Friday - the first time an international leader has visited Number 10 North. Talks on trade and continued relations are expected Downing Street said it would be the first official meeting between the PM and the Taoiseach of Ireland since Mr Burnham took office A spokesperson said the two leaders would 'discuss how the UK and Ireland can cooperate even more closely to create opportunities for people across both countries' "They are expected to focus on shared objectives including boosting trade, supporting Ukraine, and working with the European Union as Ireland continues its presidency of the EU ," Downing Street added The visit to Manchester comes days after Mr Burnham hosted Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Liverpool and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte in Oxford

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Man banned from sitting next to women and girls he doesn't know on public transport after what he did on a bus and a train Nisan Fernando Kurukulasuriya has been jailed News Amy Walker Court reporter 17:07, 17 Sep 2026 View Image Piccadilly tra A pervert who groped two teenagers on a bus was caught after exposing himself on a train. Nisan Fernando Kurukulasuriya, 39, sat next to a 17-year-old on a bus in Tameside on October 20 last year CCTV showed him putting his hand on her thigh. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Macclesfield Surrounded by police and the bomb squad, he wasn't prepared to give up, despite knowing what would be found Jonathan Wilson has been jailed View 3 Images Jonathan Wilson (Image: CTPNW/M.E.N.) News Amy Walker Court reporter 16:40, 17 Sep 2026 Surrounded by police, the bomb squad and firefighters, Jonathan Wilson wasn't prepared to give up. Soon, as he was quizzed by detectives, he would protest his innocence, despite knowing had been found inside his home. A confession The electrical engineer said he'd long had an interest in weapons and that he collected information and instructions on how to make them to 'feel safe' The truth was far more sinister. Cops searched the Macclesfield property and found knives; daggers; a machete; prohibited chemicals - potential bomb-making materials; knuckle dusters; schematics for a 3D printed firearm; manuals on how to make weapons; and a shotgun shell Materials discovered, police said, 'could potentially [have been] be used to create a homemade explosive device'. A 'large amount of literature' containing advice on how to conduct a terrorist attack was discovered Further investigations would reveal that the 49-year-old had a 'far-right, nationalist mindset'. Greater Manchester Police said he collected books on manufacturing guns and made knuckledusters using a 3D printer

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Man who downloaded vile images of children given community order Stephen Gorton received an 18 month community order and a sexual harm prevention order News Hope Gallagher 07:01, 17 Sep 2026 Updated 14:39, 17 Sep 2026 View Image Manchester Crow A man who downloaded pornographic images of children as young as three years old has been sentenced. Stephen Gorton, 37, has been sentenced to a community order for three offences of making indecent images of children across three different categories Gorton, of Central Road, Partington in Trafford , pleaded guilty to the charges on August 28 and released on bail. He appeared at Manchester Crown Court this week (September 15) for sentencing The court heard police received notification from the National Crime Agency in May 2022 with alerts about indecent images uploaded to Facebook. Gorton was not charged with distributing these images and stated that around that time his Facebook had been hacked Officers attended the defendant’s address on December 14, 2022, where they found two mobile devices which contained 32 indecent images of children. The images included an unclothed child on a bed, who was described to be aged between 3 and 5 years old Judge Recorder Lowe raised questions as to why the matter had taken so long to come to trial, with prosecutor Elizabeth Walker suggesting there were issues downloading the files from his phone and recovering the data. Ms Walker agreed there was an “excessive delay”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Batty, from Oldham, was declared missing by his grandmother in 2017, aged 11, after his mother and grandfather failed to return him from a holiday in Spain and instead moved to France He spent the following years in isolation before he was spotted by a delivery driver in December 2023 in the foothills of the Pyrenees in the south-west of the country Batty, who is now 20, said his job at a waste management company had given his young family financial security It has been a whirlwind couple of years for Batty, whose teenage years were spent living as a nomad in France His mother, Melanie, who was not his legal guardian and was heavily influenced by conspiracy theories, told him to throw away his passport They lived off-grid and he did not attend school

evidence_packet.evidence_text: "It was like two or three bombs going off," she says, recalling running to the window to look at the railway line outside "There was a train heading north and it came to a screeching halt - then seconds later another train travelling in the opposite direction hit it at speed On 19 September 1986, the village of Colwich in Staffordshire became the scene of one of the UK's most dramatic rail accidents Two intercity express trains had crashed into each other at 18:30 BST, when most villagers were settling down for dinner The 17:00 London to Manchester had passed flashing yellow lights, which, during a subsequent public inquiry it emerged the driver thought he was safe to proceed to the next signal expecting it to turn green for him In fact, he should have slowed down ready to stop. By the time the error was realised, it was too late - the emergency brake was applied and the train passed a red signal

title: Free fireworks night events to make spectacular return in Manchester

evidence_packet.title: Free fireworks night events to make spectacular return in Manchester
evidence_packet.lead: The skies over Manchester will light up once again as firework night celebrations are set to return with displays in Manchester parks this year bringing the city’s communities together
evidence_packet.summary: The skies over Manchester will light up once again as firework night celebrations are set to return with displays in Manchester parks this year bringing the city’s communities together
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The skies over Manchester will light up once again as firework night celebrations are set to return with displays in Manchester parks this year bringing the city’s communities together On Saturday 7 November, free family-friendly fireworks events at Wythenshawe Park, Heaton Park and Platt Fields Park will feature both a reduced-noise, low-impact display at 5pm for families and SEND audiences and a main fireworks display at 8pm, with accessibility and inclusivit Each of the three parks will host lantern making workshops in the weeks leading up to the events, with family-friendly lantern parades taking place ahead of the 8pm firework shows. Additional entertainment will be announced for each park in the coming weeks Major fireworks events had been paused in 2019 following the Covid-19 pandemic when funding challenges spurred a change of direction with the Council choosing to invest in a range of community focused events across the city’s parks through the autumn season – rather than the majo The good news is that these community focused events will still take place and are set to expand further in local parks this year, particularly in the run up to and during the October half term school holiday, with a mix of themed activities. Further details will be announced in With additional Council investment, the fireworks events on November 7 will be a grand finale to the community activities happening across the city

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The council has implemented a further package of cost of living assistance for residents across the borough of Rochdale who are most in need Around £15 million will be invested over the next 3 years providing a helping hand to thousands of residents in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines, and Rochdale The cost of living support, approved by councillors at a recent cabinet meeting, will utilise funding from the government’s Crisis and Resilience Fund (CRF) The fund replaces the previous Household Support Fund, providing the first multi-year funding settlement for locally delivered crisis support The CRF is a 3-year government funded programme that provides immediate support to low-income households experiencing a financial shock or significant financial hardship, while also helping to tackle the underlying causes of poverty and prevent future crisis Alongside emergency assistance, the fund will invest in services that help residents build long-term financial resilience, including welfare advice, debt support, employment opportunities and other initiatives, helping people to maximise their income and manage household costs

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

A-Kin founded by long-time friends Gasim and Sean, have become one of the city’s most exciting supper club names, turning dinners into nights built around food, music and conversation. Portfolio brings Julian Pizer back to the grills Tartuffe , as ever, will be holding the whole thing together from the grills, starting with oysters and venison, bringing in a seasonal nectarine gazpacho, and finishing their side of the menu with Alp Blossom cheese and elderberry honey before Kallos take things into dessert Tartuffe start things off with an oyster dressed with beef fat, wasabi and XO. It’s already something of a house classic, and won Best Dressed Oyster at Manchester Oyster Festival 2026. The beef fat comes from Cheshire cattle, aged and smoked before being worked into the dish

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Northern Quarter has welcomed a huge two-storey Latin BBQ restaurant, bar and music venue, brought to you by the same team behind Manchester’s beloved Firehouse and Ramona – you just know it’s going to be good with names like that Taking over the site formerly home to Pie & Ale, Dahlia has a few different concepts under one roof, but don’t let that confuse you too much Up first is Barbacoa Cósmica, an open-fire grill kitchen, with cooking inspired by Latin America and the southern states of America. evidence_packet.lead: A real project on what it actually takes to turn scattered systems into decisions you can trust Is it still worth sending an engineer to that site?
evidence_packet.summary: A real project on what it actually takes to turn scattered systems into decisions you can trust Is it still worth sending an engineer to that site? For a leader, it's a five-second question
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A real project on what it actually takes to turn scattered systems into decisions you can trust Is it still worth sending an engineer to that site? For a leader, it's a five-second question. Answering it properly, factoring in support ticket volume, engineer cost, contract terms and history, took days, several people, and still came with caveats attached Each team understood their own system perfectly well. Nobody had ever had to look across all of them for the same answer, and the larger an organisation gets, the further apart the data that should sit together ends up living This session tells the real story of an organisation that faced exactly that gap, and closed it. A fast-growing service provider with a complex, multi-system estate, each system holding good, usable data, none of it joined up. For the first time poorer people could travel regularly for a reasonable price, having a lasting effe But while the railways made travel easier, they also made the separation of the classes more pronounced, with commuter towns like Wilmslow, Alderley Edge, Sale and Cheadle Hulme spreading over farm fields. This led to a debate about the abandonment of the city by those who owed t The Railway Age got off to an inauspicious start with an angry crowd in Manchester protesting about the price of food and about the lack of representation. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
